operational_issue: The old manuscript ambiguously presented itself as an empirical diagnostic paper although only estimand definitions and printed arithmetic were independently checkable.
locations_checked: Old manuscript: title, abstract, introduction, evidence boundary, estimand, results, ancillary analysis, limitations, conclusion, and references

Revised manuscript: title, abstract, introduction and contribution list, measurement-status paragraph, Section 2 audit partition and missing-evidence inventory, Section 3 estimand, Section 4 source-reported results, Section 5 contribution boundary, Section 6 limitations and availability, conclusion, and references
Complete revised source and all supplied evidence/provenance records
Paper-wide searches for language implying new measurement, experimentation, reproduction, or independent empirical verification
reasoning_summary: The revision has a coherent non-empirical identity throughout: the title and all major narrative sections call it an evidence-and-estimand audit. It explicitly limits the independently checked subset to estimand definitions, internal formal structure, and arithmetic printed from transcribed values. All empirical values, counts, and doses are globally labeled source-reported and not independently verifiable; the two retained records are also labeled individually in the results tables. The abstract states that no experiment was run, and the availability section states that no empirical value was rerun or independently recomputed. The manuscript identifies the unavailable item records, intervention details, sample construction, prompts, decode traces, score construction, implementation, analysis code, revisions, and environment information. The supplied claim map, provenance table, and experiment registry consistently classify the retained measurements as source-reported and not rerun. No revised passage presents an empirical value as newly measured, reproduced, or independently verified.
